glosses: A competitor (person, team, company, etc.) with the same goal as another, or striving to attain the same thing. Defeating a rival may be a primary or necessary goal of a competitor.

examples.text: Chris is my biggest rival in the 400-metre race.
Every day is like survival / You're my lover, not my rival

Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you[…] "share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.

glosses: Someone or something with similar claims of quality or distinction as another.

examples.text: As a social historian, he has no rival.

glosses: One having a common right or privilege with another; a partner.

examples.text: If you do meet Horatio and Marcellus, / The rivals of my watch, bid them make haste.

glosses: Having the same pretensions or claims; standing in competition for superiority.

examples.text: rival lovers

glosses: To oppose or compete with.

examples.text: to rival somebody in love

glosses: To be equal to, or match, or to surpass another.

examples.text: But the Waverley is still the best-placed station of any British city, and gives the arriving stranger a first impression rivalled in Europe only by the exclusively watery station approach at Venice.

glosses: To strive to equal or excel; to emulate.

glosses: Rivalidad o controversia que hay entre dos o más personas u organismos sobre algún punto. Ej. (organismos): Estas dos plantas están estableciendo una competencia por la luz.
Lucha o riña que existe entre dos o más personas que desean obtener el mismo fin u objetivo.
Dícese acerca del grupo rival. Ej.: Juan ahora es de la competencia y antes era de los nuestros.
Por extensión, situación en que dos o más empresas ofrecen el mismo servicio para lograr el mismo objetivo.

examples.text: Es difícil que te lleguen clientes porque a lo que te dedicas tiene demasiada competencia

One who pursues someone, especially a woman, for a romantic relationship or marriage; a wooer; one who falls in love with or courts someone.

examples.text: (Notice that "Lysias" begins from the realistic assumption that an attractive young man with many suitors will "gratify" one of them, the only question being which. Rightly or wrongly, he treats the question, "Shall I at all?" as already resolved.)

examples.text: […] and Mortimer asserted he had no shortage of suitors ready, willing, and able to make acquisition loans […]

glosses: A party to a suit or litigation.
One who sues, petitions, solicits, or entreats; a petitioner.
To play the suitor; to woo; to make love.
Someone who woos or courts.

examples.text: Penelope for her Vliſſes ſake, / Deuiz'd a VVeb her vvooers to deceaue: / in vvhich the vvorke that ſhe all day did make / the ſame at night ſhe did againe vnreaue, […]
